reference: No matching GNU sqlite command-line program is available for this Bash builtin API. These are contract checks, not GNU parity: metadata stdout follows the builtin's documented help; SQL result expectations are derived from SQLite 3.47.2 SQL semantics and the documented tab-separated row contract. Error wording is deliberately checked only for nonempty stderr.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and documented help text (metadata only).
In-memory open/close, typed TEXT/INTEGER/REAL/NULL/BLOB bindings, and row conversion.
Prepared insert with quoted text, changes/rowid reporting, and persistence after closing and reopening a relative fixture database.
Multirow stepping, SQLITE_DONE status, statement reset, and clearing bindings on reset.
SQL exec error status and continued usability of the database handle.
Invalid BLOB hex rejection, documented statement auto-finalization, and empty BLOB typing.
Close refusal while a prepared statement remains active, followed by successful use and cleanup.
exclusions: Concurrent file writers and lock contention are deferred because the documented unix-none file VFS has no interprocess locking.
BLOB values containing NUL bytes in row output and ambiguous tab/newline field serialization are not covered.
Handle-table exhaustion and multiple simultaneous database connections are outside this small deterministic suite.
No case is labeled GNU parity because there is no matching sqlite CLI; no external CLI is substituted.

cases.purpose: Check the Bash builtin type and exact documented help surface without counting metadata as operation coverage.
cases.stdout:
builtin
sqlite: sqlite
    SQLite handle API for bash-os.
      sqlite open PATH -h DB_VAR
      sqlite exec DB SQL
      sqlite prepare DB SQL -h STMT_VAR
      sqlite bind STMT N VALUE [-t TEXT|INTEGER|REAL|NULL|BLOB]
      sqlite step STMT [-V ROW_VAR]
      sqlite reset|finalize STMT
      sqlite close DB
      sqlite transaction DB BEGIN|COMMIT|ROLLBACK
      sqlite changes DB
      sqlite last-insert-rowid DB
      sqlite --stats             # print active_stmts and max_stmts
    
      (file databases use unix-none VFS, memory SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX; no locking)
      bind failure auto-finalizes the prepared statement (slot reclaimed).

cases.purpose: Check the documented bind types and tab-separated row conversion using a single deterministic in-memory SELECT.
cases.script:
sqlite open :memory: -h db
sqlite prepare "$db" 'SELECT typeof(?1), ?1, typeof(?2), ?2, typeof(?3), ?3, typeof(?4), ?4, typeof(?5), length(?5), hex(?5)' -h st
sqlite bind "$st" 1 'row text'
sqlite bind "$st" 2 42 -t INTEGER
sqlite bind "$st" 3 2.5 -t REAL
sqlite bind "$st" 4 ignored -t NULL
sqlite bind "$st" 5 410042 -t BLOB
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf '%s\n' "$row"
sqlite finalize "$st"
sqlite close "$db"
cases.stdout: text	row text	integer	42	real	2.5	null		blob	3	410042

cases.purpose: Check prepared text insertion, changes and rowid reporting, and persistence after closing and reopening a relative fixture database.
cases.script:
sqlite open records.db -h db
sqlite exec "$db" 'CREATE TABLE records (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT UNIQUE)'
sqlite prepare "$db" 'INSERT INTO records(value) VALUES (?1)' -h ins
sqlite bind "$ins" 1 "O'Reilly & sons"
if sqlite step "$ins"; then exit 90; else step_rc=$?; fi
[[ $step_rc -eq 1 ]]
printf 'changes=%s rowid=%s\n' "$(sqlite changes "$db")" "$(sqlite last-insert-rowid "$db")"
sqlite finalize "$ins"
sqlite close "$db"
sqlite open records.db -h db
sqlite prepare "$db" 'SELECT id, value FROM records' -h sel
sqlite step "$sel" -V row
printf 'row=%s\n' "$row"
sqlite finalize "$sel"
sqlite close "$db"

cases.purpose: Check that rollback removes an uncommitted insert and commit preserves the following insert.
cases.script:
sqlite open :memory: -h db
sqlite exec "$db" 'CREATE TABLE records (value TEXT)'
sqlite transaction "$db" BEGIN
sqlite exec "$db" "INSERT INTO records VALUES ('rolled back')"
sqlite transaction "$db" ROLLBACK
sqlite transaction "$db" BEGIN
sqlite exec "$db" "INSERT INTO records VALUES ('kept')"
sqlite transaction "$db" COMMIT
sqlite prepare "$db" 'SELECT count(*), min(value), max(value) FROM records' -h st
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf '%s\n' "$row"
sqlite finalize "$st"
sqlite close "$db"

cases.purpose: Check ordered row streaming, the no-more-rows status, statement rewind, and reset's documented binding clear.
cases.script:
sqlite open :memory: -h db
sqlite exec "$db" 'CREATE TABLE n (v INTEGER); INSERT INTO n VALUES (3),(1),(2)'
sqlite prepare "$db" 'SELECT v FROM n ORDER BY v' -h st
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf '%s\n' "$row"
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf '%s\n' "$row"
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf '%s\n' "$row"
if sqlite step "$st"; then exit 91; else step_rc=$?; fi
[[ $step_rc -eq 1 ]]
sqlite reset "$st"
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf '%s\n' "$row"
sqlite finalize "$st"
sqlite prepare "$db" 'SELECT ?1' -h st
sqlite bind "$st" 1 before-reset
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf 'bound=<%s>\n' "$row"
sqlite reset "$st"
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf 'cleared=<%s>\n' "$row"
sqlite finalize "$st"
sqlite close "$db"

cases.purpose: Check nonzero SQL execution failure and that a failed statement leaves the open database usable.
cases.script:
sqlite open :memory: -h db
if sqlite exec "$db" 'SELECT * FROM absent_table'; then exit 92; else sql_rc=$?; fi
[[ $sql_rc -eq 1 ]]
sqlite exec "$db" 'CREATE TABLE valid (v INTEGER); INSERT INTO valid VALUES (7)'
sqlite prepare "$db" 'SELECT v FROM valid' -h st
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf '%s\n' "$row"
sqlite finalize "$st"
sqlite close "$db"

cases.purpose: Check rejection of non-hex BLOB input, documented automatic statement reclamation, and the empty BLOB representation.
cases.script:
sqlite open :memory: -h db
sqlite prepare "$db" 'SELECT ?1' -h bad
if sqlite bind "$bad" 1 0g -t BLOB; then exit 93; else bind_rc=$?; fi
[[ $bind_rc -eq 2 ]]
sqlite --stats
sqlite prepare "$db" 'SELECT typeof(?1), length(?1)' -h st
sqlite bind "$st" 1 '' -t BLOB
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf '%s\n' "$row"
sqlite finalize "$st"
sqlite close "$db"

cases.purpose: Check the close precondition for unfinalized statements and verify the database handle remains usable after the rejected close.
cases.script:
sqlite open :memory: -h db
sqlite prepare "$db" 'SELECT 1' -h st
if sqlite close "$db"; then exit 94; else close_rc=$?; fi
[[ $close_rc -eq 1 ]]
sqlite step "$st" -V row
printf '%s\n' "$row"
sqlite finalize "$st"
sqlite close "$db"

cases.purpose: Record the unsupported concurrent-writer/lock-contention scenario without making concurrent writes to the unlocked VFS.
Two independent in-memory connections retain separate SQL state; a closed handle fails with usage status and diagnostic.
cases.script:
sqlite open :memory: -h first
sqlite open :memory: -h second
sqlite exec "$first" 'CREATE TABLE t(v); INSERT INTO t VALUES(1)'
sqlite exec "$second" 'CREATE TABLE t(v); INSERT INTO t VALUES(2)'
for db in "$first" "$second"; do
 sqlite prepare "$db" 'SELECT v FROM t' -h st
 sqlite step "$st" -V row
 printf '%s\n' "$row"
 sqlite finalize "$st"
done
sqlite close "$first"
if sqlite exec "$first" 'SELECT 1'; then exit 90; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 2 ]]
sqlite close "$second"
